competitors.name: In-house 'website VIN vs floorplan VIN' comparison (SAS Global Forum paper, 'PROC HTTP: Using the Web to Combat Fraud in Auto Finance During a Global Pandemic')
competitors.what_they_do: Closest prior art. Per the search-result summary (the page returned 403, so I could not read it), a lender-side team scraped VINs from dealers' advertised web inventory and compared them to the lender's active floorplan VINs to spot fraud when physical audits were disrupted. It is a method in a conference paper, not a sold product, but it shows large lenders can and do build the core signal themselves.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Not a company. In-house or academic. Not verified beyond the search snippet.

competitors.name: Vero Technologies (VeroOS)
competitors.what_they_do: AI-native wholesale/floorplan lending platform with 12 modules including Audits, Risk, Titles and Vero AI, plus 40+ integrations. Its blog series 'Under the Floor' and posts on Sky Auto and double-flooring target this exact pain (bunching, bulking and payoff patterns around audits, single-lender blind spots). Its stated monitoring is payment, NSF and open-banking based, with no public-listing disappearance signal found. It is the most likely platform to add this as a feature.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Funding not found. Offices in 4 locations, named C-suite and VP team. Actively selling to banks, captives and independents.

competitors.name: SBS Digital Audit (SBS Software)
competitors.what_they_do: Hybrid/photo-based floorplan audit software marketed as cutting audit cost and dealer risk. This attacks the 'audits are too infrequent' pain from the audit side rather than by inferring risk from listings.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Per a Vero article, more than 100,000 digital audits across US dealerships by end of 2025 (2.5 to 3M verification images a year). Established core-banking and asset-finance vendor.

competitors.name: LotCount
competitors.what_they_do: Digital dealer inventory control with VIN-level reconciliation reports (timestamps, sites, photo evidence) delivered within 48 hours, described in search results as accepted by floorplan funders as audit evidence. The page itself could not be fetched, so details are from the search snippet.

competitors.name: NextGear Capital (Cox Automotive)
competitors.what_they_do: Large independent-dealer floorplan lender. Per Vero's article it launched an in-app dealer self-audit feature in late 2024 with AI/API reconciliation. Its parent Cox Automotive also owns Autotrader, vAuto and Dealertrack, so it holds both listing data and floorplan books. I found no public SOT-from-listings product, but this is the biggest latent incumbent risk.

competitors.name: Collateral Specialists Inc. (CSI)
competitors.what_they_do: Field floorplan inspections plus on-site 'dealer monitoring' for high-risk or out-of-trust dealers (daily inspection, key and title lockbox, tracking sale proceeds). This is the manual incumbent workflow the idea would triage or replace.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established services firm. Funding not found.

competitors.name: Netresult Mobility AutoAudit
competitors.what_they_do: Mobile audit app that loads the dealer manifest, lets auditors search by VIN, and uploads results to the lender's wholesale finance system.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Small vendor based in Christchurch, NZ.

competitors.name: MarketCheck
competitors.what_they_do: Data supplier and potential competitor. Scans over 100,000 dealer websites daily across the US, Canada and the UK, and sells APIs, feeds and reports. Its site does not mention listing-history or delisted-VIN products for lenders, though it could add one. It is also the obvious licensed data source for the idea's listing feed.

competitors.name: DRN (Digital Recognition Network) DRNsights
competitors.what_they_do: License-plate-reader vehicle sighting data and alerts for lenders, insurers and recovery, including fraud investigations. It is an alternative physical-location signal, not listing-based.

competitors.name: MOBI Dealer Floorplan Audit pilot
competitors.what_they_do: Consortium pilot using zero-knowledge proof of vehicle location from telematics to automate floorplan audits. Contributors include Ford Credit, GM Financial, Stellantis Financial Services, Nissan Motor Acceptance, BMW Bank and RouteOne. It shows the big captives want automated audit signals, but it is a pilot and not a commercial product.

competitors.name: Core floorplan platforms (Solifi, Alfa Systems, Soft4Leasing, Odessa, DataScan RiskGauge)
competitors.what_they_do: Servicing and platform vendors with stock-audit workflows and risk dashboards. The May 2026 roundup lists none as addressing sold-out-of-trust detection explicitly. DataScan's RiskGauge is marketed for inventory risk, but I could not verify it.

white_space: Among the products I could find, none sells the specific signal in this idea: an external-behavior signal (a floored VIN vanishing from the dealer site or marketplaces) checked against the lender's own payoff ledger on a running clock, with a ranked daily queue. Existing offerings cover other things. Physical or photo audits (CSI, LotCount, SBS Digital Audit, Netresult) are periodic and dealer-cooperative. Platforms (Vero, Solifi, Alfa, SBS servicing) analyze the lender's own payment and title data. Bank-data tools (Plaid-style) watch dealer cash. DRN covers location. The unserved wedge is mid-size and small lenders that lack data-science teams: independent floorplan companies, credit unions and community banks with dealer lines, and third-party audit firms that need risk-based audit targeting. It is strongest for used-car and buy-here-pay-here dealers, where captives' retail-delivery reports do not exist. Caveats that shrink the white space: (1) captives see retail deliveries within days and can build the signal in-house, and the SAS paper suggests at least one lender did; (2) Vero, SBS and Cox/NextGear could bolt on the signal; (3) a listing that disappears is a noisy signal (wholesaled, transferred, in recon, or the dealer never lists), so precision must be proven; (4) marketplace scraping has terms-of-service risk, so a licensed feed such as MarketCheck is likely needed.
evidence_of_demand: Strong evidence that the problem is real and that lenders spend on adjacent controls. None found that anyone pays for this exact signal. (1) The Sky Auto Mall case: Ford Credit and Stellantis Financial sued over floorplan fraud and out-of-trust sales. Stellantis claims more than $12.3M and about $1.4M in unreturned sale proceeds. Ford claims $6.6M. Ford found 81 double-financed units only after Stellantis tipped it off and it compared lists. The dealer group then filed for bankruptcy. Sources: https://www.carscoops.com/2026/03/iowa-stellantis-ford-dealer/ , https://www.autonews.com/retail/an-stellantis-ford-captives-sue-iowa-dealership-out-of-trust-0317/ (page returned 403; seen only in search results), https://www.autofinancenews.net/allposts/risk-management/sky-auto-mall-owners-file-for-bankruptcy-amid-18m-floorplan-fraud-lawsuits/ (page returned 403; seen only in search results). Note that the fraud was mainly double-flooring, which listing disappearance would not catch. Only the sold-without-payoff part fits the idea. (2) Vendors are marketing directly at this pain. Vero published a floorplan fraud series (April 2026) that says physical audits are snapshots, that 10 to 15% of inventory turns between 30 to 45 day audit cycles, and that lenders lack cross-lender visibility. Sources: https://www.vero-technologies.com/news/the-hidden-mechanics-behind-double-flooring-what-recent-dealership-fraud-stories-actually-show and https://www.vero-technologies.com/news/how-a-single-fraud-story-exposed-a-systemic-floorplan-blind-spot . (3) Spend on audit workarounds is large. SBS reports more than 100,000 digital audits in the US by end 2025, per https://www.vero-technologies.com/news/ai-in-wholesale-finance-whats-actually-happening-on-the-ground , which also says dealer-services teams at banks want to 'automate audit triage and SOT reporting'. A March 2026 Young & Associates piece says audits are tedious, that discrepancies found after weeks or months raise loss severity, and describes a double-floored dealer found by audit: https://www.younginc.com/blog/the-importance-of-floor-plan-audits-for-lending-institutions/ . MOBI says lenders hold reserves because audits are infrequent, and a consortium including Ford Credit, GM Financial and Stellantis piloted automated audit tech: https://dlt.mobi/dfa/ . (4) The 'audit-triage' framing is supported, but I found no RFPs, pricing pages or forum posts showing lenders paying $15 to $30 per dealer per month for listing-based monitoring. That price point is unvalidated. Research limits: the web-search budget ran out after 4 searches, and several pages (LotCount, AFC, SAS paper, Solifi) could not be fetched. I did not check Crunchbase, YC or Product Hunt, and GitHub repository searches for open-source tools returned nothing.
sharper_angle: Do not sell a standalone 'radar' dashboard. Sell it as an audit-targeting and triage layer that turns the listing-disappearance-plus-missing-payoff signal into a daily ranked list of specific VINs to verify within 24 to 48 hours. Sell it through channels that already own the lender relationship: (a) as a signal module or partner integration for the audit vendors and platforms (SBS Digital Audit, LotCount, CSI, Vero, Solifi), which turns the platforms from likely competitors into distributors, and (b) direct to independent floorplan lenders, credit unions and community banks with used-car and BHPH dealers, where there are no captive retail-delivery reports and no data-science team. Price per verified catch or per audit-hour saved, not a flat $20 per dealer. The proof to lead with is a backtest showing what share of already-confirmed SOT cases the signal flagged, and the false-positive rate, since delisting is noisy. Then add the piece no single-lender tool has: a cross-lender check that flags a VIN floored with two lenders while still publicly listed. Vero itself names single-lender visibility as the blind spot. Use a licensed listing feed such as MarketCheck to avoid scraping and terms-of-service risk. Treat the dealer-facing 'fix your unpaid VINs' view and the contracts-in-transit tracker as a later upsell, not the wedge. Before building, spend two weeks re-running the incumbent check with unrestricted search (Crunchbase, YC, Product Hunt, Cox/NextGear and AFC/OPENLANE product pages) and interview five lender risk or audit heads to confirm the signal would change their audit order.
